newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up, carloads flat from yr ago.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up, carloads flat from yr ago.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic as measured in intermodal rose 5.2 percent in the week ended October 12 from the same week a year ago while carload volume was flat, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said intermodal traffic, which does not include carloads, totaled 173,541 trailers and containers in the October 12 week compared with 165,039 in the year-ago week.

Carloads stood at 357,864 last week compared with 357,708 in the same 1995 week. But ton-miles rose 1.1 percent to 26.6 billion from 26.3 billion last year. A ton mile is equal to one ton of freight hauled one mile.

"The continued strength in intermodal is very encouraging," Harvey Levine, AAR chief economist, said. "This past week was the fifth busiest ever and was up more than 4,000 units from the comparable week two years ago, when the current intermodal records were set."

AAR said the biggest carload increases were in farm products excluding grain, which climbed 11.4 percent to 2,030 from 1,822 a year ago, and petroleum, which was up 8.5 percent to 5,637 carloads from 5,197.
Coal loadings stood at 138,491, a 3.4 percent rise from 133,999 last year, while motor vehicles and equipment were up 2.4 percent to 21,923 carloads from 21,403.

But grain loadings fell 9.5 percent to 24,064 carloads from 26,596 last year. Primary forest products declined 11.9 percent to 7,546 carloads from 8,561, while metals and products dropped 9.1 percent to 11,535 in the week from 12,686 last year.
In the first 41 weeks of 1996, AAR said ton-miles rose 1.9 percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic also rose 1.2 percent, but carloads fell 0.8 percent, AAR said.
